classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b identify sine's endpoint behaviour; part c requires choosing a fixed hypotenuse and connecting changing triangle geometry to the opposite-to-hypotenuse ratio, without that representation being supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What happens to the value of $\sin\theta$ as $\theta$ gets closer and closer to $0^\circ$?

answer.worked: With the hypotenuse fixed, the opposite side tends to zero as $\theta$ approaches $0^\circ$. Thus $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$ tends to 0.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What happens to the value of $\sin\theta$ as $\theta$ gets closer and closer to $90^\circ$?

answer.worked: With the hypotenuse fixed, the opposite side approaches the hypotenuse length as $\theta$ approaches $90^\circ$. Thus $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$ tends to 1.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Can you explain why the value of $\sin\theta$ behaves like this?

answer.short: With a fixed hypotenuse, the opposite side tends to zero as the angle approaches $0^\circ$, and to the hypotenuse length as the angle approaches $90^\circ$.
answer.worked: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$. Keep the hypotenuse length fixed. As $\theta$ approaches $0^\circ$, the opposite side tends to zero, so the ratio tends to 0. As $\theta$ approaches $90^\circ$, the opposite side approaches the hypotenuse length, so the ratio tends to 1.
